title: Grok (chatbot)
text:
Grok is a generative artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot developed by xAI (now operating under the brand SpaceXSI), an AI company founded by Elon Musk in March 2023 to advance scientific discovery and understand the nature of the universe, and acquired by SpaceX on February 2, 2026.
The logo depicts a black hole with its accretion disk, stylized to form the letter 'G'.
xAI launched Grok in beta on November 3, 2023. It draws inspiration from the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy and answers almost any question while suggesting related ones. Grok pulls real-time knowledge from the X platform (formerly Twitter). As of October 2026 its flagship model is Grok 4.7.

Unlike many rival AI systems, Grok prioritizes maximal truthfulness. It includes humor, handles edgy or rejected queries with a rebellious streak, and resists standard political biases. As an artificial intelligence, Grok does not have personal religious beliefs or affiliations.

Grok features X integration for current events, fewer safety restrictions than competitors, and a focus on facts over ideology. This approach draws praise for honesty but criticism for unfiltered outputs.

#Origins

#Founding of xAI

xAI was incorporated in Nevada on March 9, 2023, by Elon Musk, who served as the primary founder and leader of the venture. The company was formally announced to the public on July 12, 2023, via a dedicated website and social media posts, positioning itself as an AI initiative aimed at competing with established players like OpenAI.

Musk's motivation stemmed from concerns over the direction of existing AI development, particularly what he described as insufficient emphasis on truth-seeking and scientific advancement in competitors influenced by profit-driven or ideologically skewed priorities.

The stated mission of xAI at founding was to "understand the true nature of the universe," emphasizing rigorous pursuit of fundamental truths through AI rather than narrow commercial applications. This objective reflected Musk's broader vision for AI as a tool for accelerating human scientific discovery, drawing from his experiences with prior ventures like Tesla and SpaceX. Unlike some contemporaries, xAI was structured to prioritize curiosity-driven research over immediate monetization, with Musk personally funding the initial operations. The first disclosed external equity sales, amounting to $134.7 million out of a $1 billion offering, occurred starting November 29, 2023, as reported in the company's December 5, 2023, SEC Form D filing.
On January 6, 2026, xAI raised $20 billion in an upsized Series E funding round.

The initial team consisted of Elon Musk plus 11 members recruited primarily from leading AI research institutions to build core capabilities in machine learning and large-scale model training. Key early hires included Igor Babuschkin, a former Google DeepMind engineer recruited as a founding member and later serving as chief engineer, along with alumni from OpenAI, Google Research, Microsoft Research, and Tesla. Other notable founding contributors encompassed specialists like Manuel Kroiss, Yuhuai Wu, Christian Szegedy, and Toby Pohlen, who brought expertise in areas such as reinforcement learning and scalable AI systems from their tenures at Google and Google DeepMind. This assembly was designed to leverage proven technical talent while avoiding the bureaucratic constraints Musk criticized in larger tech organizations.

On February 2, 2026, SpaceX acquired xAI in a deal valuing xAI at $250 billion and the combined entity at $1.25 trillion, integrating Grok under SpaceX.

#Inspirations from Prior AI Initiatives

Elon Musk co-founded OpenAI in December 2015 as a non-profit aimed at building artificial general intelligence (AGI)—AI that matches or exceeds human intelligence across tasks—with a focus on safety and broad human benefit. His motivation stemmed from fears that companies like Google might advance AI without safeguards. Musk left OpenAI's board in February 2018, citing conflicts with Tesla's AI work. He disagreed with the group's shift toward commercial goals; OpenAI later adopted a capped-profit model in March 2019. These events fueled Musk's concerns that profit-driven approaches and strict safety rules could limit honest AI inquiry.

OpenAI's ChatGPT launch on November 30, 2022, sharpened Musk's criticisms. He called it politically biased, claiming its training data spread falsehoods to match institutional views over facts. In April 2023, Musk proposed "TruthGPT," an AI focused on truth-seeking without what he saw as "politically correct" limits in models like ChatGPT or Anthropic's Claude. OpenAI's move from open-source roots to closed, moderated systems spurred xAI's creation in Nevada in March 2023, announced publicly on July 12, 2023. Grok launched in November 2023 as xAI's main chatbot, emphasizing raw reasoning from basic principles rather than filtered replies.

Grok's design learns from flaws in earlier large language models, like how safety tweaks made them prone to errors similar to biases in media or academic data, per Musk. Unlike ChatGPT, which added web browsing on September 27, 2023, to update beyond its training cutoff and avoid harm—leading to outputs Musk deemed evasive or slanted—Grok pulls real-time data from X (formerly Twitter) for evidence-based answers. xAI open-sourced Grok-1's weights in March 2024 to boost transparency, unlike closed rivals. This approach seeks to fix past AI's focus on caution over causal realism and empirical checks.

#Design Philosophy: Maximal Truth-Seeking

Grok and ChatGPT logos displayed side by side

Grok's design centers on maximal truth-seeking. This means the AI pursues objective facts and direct insights, free from ideological limits. xAI built Grok with inspiration from The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. It features a witty but evidence-driven style to probe real-world complexities.

This approach differs from many large language models. xAI views those models' safety features and alignment as sources of bias toward dominant cultural views.

Grok favors verifiable data over popular opinion. It challenges common views if evidence or logic supports it. Elon Musk describes Grok as a "maximally truth-seeking AI, even if that truth is sometimes at odds with what is politically correct." xAI seeks to counter biases from politicized training data in rivals like OpenAI.

xAI's system prompts, including versions published through 2025 and 2026, direct Grok toward neutral, useful responses across political views. Grok trains on public and curated datasets. At response time, it adds real-time data from X to link outputs to current events, building on pre-trained knowledge.

This enables "unfiltered answers." Grok avoids automatic censorship and gives straightforward replies to tough questions.

The design also stresses wide access. xAI avoids moral lectures, focusing on practical value for all users. Musk links this to "woke" biases in other AIs, which he sees as over-aligned with progressive sources that skew facts.

Grok scores well on benchmarks like GSM8K for math, MMLU for knowledge, and HumanEval for coding. At launch, it showed progressive biases from internet data, as Musk noted. xAI plans ongoing tweaks to strengthen truth-seeking while curbing misuse.

#Safety Features, Guardrails, and Risk Management

Grok incorporates several safety mechanisms, though designed with fewer content restrictions than many competing AI models to prioritize truthfulness and helpfulness on controversial topics.

#Core Safety Policies

Basic refusal policy: Grok declines to assist with clear intent to engage in criminal activity posing severe harm, such as detailed instructions for violence or weapons development.

Heightened safeguards: For queries posing foreseeable non-trivial risk of catastrophic malicious use (e.g., weapons of mass destruction, large-scale violence, terrorism, or major cyber attacks causing over 100 deaths or $1 billion in damages), advanced protections apply, including potential response limitations.

xAI Risk Management Framework (RMF) and successor FAIF: The August 2025 RMF outlined risk handling for model development and deployment, targeting an answer rate of less than 1 in 20 on restricted queries for dangerous capabilities. It was succeeded by the Frontier Artificial Intelligence Framework (FAIF) effective 30 June 2026. Models are trained for honesty, controllability, and instruction hierarchy obedience. Public deployment on X enables real-time monitoring and rapid response to emerging risks.

#Acceptable Use Policy

Users must comply with xAI's Acceptable Use Policy, prohibiting harm to people or property, law violations, guardrail circumvention (except approved red-teaming), and misleading about AI outputs. Suspected child sexual abuse material is reported to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children.

#Image Generation Restrictions

Following 2026 controversies over non-consensual deepfakes, xAI restricted Grok's image editing and generation features, including blocks on edits of real people in revealing clothing, geoblocking in certain jurisdictions, and limiting some capabilities to paid users.

#Kids/Teens Safety

Minimum age is 13 (with guardian permission for minors). A "Kids Mode" exists with content filters and parental controls, though independent assessments (e.g., Common Sense Media 2026 report) have criticized its effectiveness in preventing exposure to inappropriate material.

Grok's philosophy emphasizes safety through targeted refusals on severe harm while avoiding broad censorship, enabling open discussion within legal and ethical bounds. For privacy, conversations may be reviewed for safety and improvement; users should avoid sharing sensitive data and can opt out of training use via settings.

#List of Grok Models

xAI has released several Grok versions. Only the initial Grok-1 model weights are open-source under the Apache 2.0 license; later models, including the Grok-4.x series as of 2026, are proprietary. Key releases include Grok-1.5 (text-only, March 2024), Grok-1.5V (vision preview for testers, April 2024), Grok-2 (public vision capabilities, August 2024), Grok-3 (reasoning emphasis, February 2025), Grok-4 (leading benchmarks like ARC-AGI with tool use and real-time search, July 2025), Grok-4.1 and Grok-4.1 Fast (November 19, 2025), with Grok-4.20 Beta 2 (March 3, 2026), and the Grok Imagine API (January 28, 2026). The Grok Imagine API introduced advanced video generation and editing capabilities, including text and image-to-video conversion, cinematic motion, object addition/removal/swapping, scene transformations (e.g., weather or time changes), precise color and object editing, restyling (e.g., cyberpunk, anime), and sketch-to-animation. These updates, powered by extensive compute resources, position Grok as a leading AI performer for tasks such as image generation, multimodal processing, and advanced text-to-video generation.

As of October 2026, the current flagship Grok model is Grok 4.7, announced by xAI on September 21, 2026 as its most powerful model for coding and knowledge work; it followed Grok 4.6 and Grok 4.20. Active variants include grok-4.7 via API, alongside user-selectable modes featuring Grok 4.7.

#Grok-0 (August 2023)

Grok-0 was xAI's initial prototype large language model, featuring a dense transformer architecture with 33 billion parameters. Completed on August 18, 2023, it approached the performance of Meta's LLaMA 2 (70B) on benchmarks such as GSM8k (56.8%), MMLU (65.7%), and HumanEval (39.7%), despite using only half the training resources. This early model informed the architectural and training approaches for subsequent Grok iterations, including Grok-1.

#Grok-1 (November 2023)

Grok-1 served as the foundational large language model for the Grok chatbot, with xAI announcing limited early access to a prototype on November 3, 2023, for a small number of U.S. users. Broader access to X Premium+ subscribers was announced in November 2023, with rollout completed around December 8, 2023, and expansion to all X Premium subscribers occurring on March 26, 2024. Developed entirely from scratch by xAI without reliance on external pretrained models, it represented the company's first production-scale effort following its initial prototype, Grok-0. At launch, xAI positioned Grok-1 as competitive with contemporary models like OpenAI's GPT-3.5 in areas such as real-world knowledge and reasoning, emphasizing its training on diverse public data sources up to Q3 2023 to prioritize factual accuracy over censorship.

The model's architecture, a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) design with 314 billion total parameters—activating approximately 25% (86 billion) per token via 8 experts (2 active per forward pass)—along with 64 transformer layers, was detailed upon its open-sourcing in March 2024, while the context length of 8,192 tokens had been disclosed in the November 3, 2023 model card. This MoE structure enabled efficient scaling by routing inputs selectively, diverging from dense transformer architectures dominant in peers like GPT series models. Training leveraged xAI's custom stack built on JAX and Rust, utilizing thousands of GPUs, though exact compute details remained proprietary.

Post-launch evaluations highlighted Grok-1's strengths in uncensored responses and humor-infused outputs, but also limitations in areas like coding and mathematics compared to closed-source leaders; for instance, it scored 63.2% on HumanEval (coding) and 62.9% on GSM8K (math), trailing GPT-4 but surpassing some open models. xAI released the raw base model weights and architecture under the Apache 2.0 license on March 17, 2024, excluding fine-tuning code or datasets to encourage community experimentation while protecting proprietary training methods. This openness contrasted with competitors' approaches, aligning with xAI's stated goal of accelerating scientific understanding through accessible AI foundations, though critics noted the absence of training reproducibility as a barrier to full verification.

#Grok-1.5 (March 2024)

Grok-1.5, released by xAI on March 28, 2024, represents an iterative advancement over the initial Grok-1 model, with enhancements primarily in reasoning capabilities, long-context processing, and performance on mathematical and coding benchmarks. The model supports a context length of 128,000 tokens, enabling it to handle extended inputs such as entire source code files or lengthy documents, which xAI reported as a 16-fold increase in effective memory capacity compared to Grok-1.

In evaluations conducted by xAI, Grok-1.5 demonstrated superior results on standardized benchmarks for mathematical reasoning and code generation. It achieved 50.6% accuracy on the MATH benchmark, which tests competition-level mathematics problems, more than doubling the performance of Grok-1. On the GSM8K benchmark for grade-school math word problems, it scored 90%. For coding tasks, Grok-1.5 attained 74.1% on HumanEval, a measure of functional correctness in Python code generation, outperforming Grok-1 and approaching contemporary models like GPT-4.

xAI subsequently introduced Grok-1.5V, a multimodal variant previewed on April 12, 2024, that extends the model's capabilities to process visual inputs alongside text. However, Grok-1.5V was not released to the public, remaining available only to early testers and existing Grok users, with no subsequent full public rollout announced. Grok-1.5V can analyze images such as diagrams, photographs, and screenshots to perform tasks like translating visual content into executable code or reasoning about real-world spatial understanding, as evidenced by its top performance on the RealWorldQA benchmark for spatial tasks. This version marked xAI's entry into vision-enabled AI, with applications demonstrated in converting block diagrams to Python code and interpreting charts.

#Grok-2 (August 2024)

Grok-2, released by xAI on August 13, 2024, as an early beta preview, represents a major upgrade from Grok-1.5, with enhanced performance in reasoning, tool use, chat interactions, coding, and vision processing. The model integrates real-time information access and multimodal vision capabilities for tasks such as visual mathematics solving and document question-answering; image generation was added via a collaboration with Black Forest Labs using the FLUX.1 model. A smaller variant, Grok-2 mini, accompanies it, delivering comparable functionality with lower resource demands.

On standardized benchmarks, Grok-2 outperforms Grok-1.5 across key areas including graduate-level science reasoning (GPQA), multitask language understanding (MMLU), mathematical problem-solving (MATH), and visual mathematical reasoning (MathVista), as shown below:

Initial access was limited to X Premium and Premium+ subscribers, with an enterprise API public beta launched on November 4, 2024 (with initial grok-beta available from October 21, 2024). On December 6, 2024, following limited regional testing in November 2024, xAI enabled access to Grok-2 for free users on X with usage limits such as 10 messages every 2 hours. Aurora first appeared for users on December 7, 2024, was briefly pulled, and was formally announced by xAI on December 9, 2024, for rollout within a week, integrating the autoregressive image generation model for photorealistic image generation. On December 12, 2024, xAI released a refined, three-times-faster version with improved accuracy, instruction adherence, and multilingual support, building on the free access rollout that began on December 6, 2024, and set pricing for the new Grok-2 family models (e.g., grok-2-1212 and grok-2-vision-1212) at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, reduced from the $5 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens of the earlier October 2024 grok-beta API preview. This update highlighted and further improved web search functionality (first introduced on November 16, 2024) and source citations (introduced later).

#Grok-3 (February 2025)

xAI released Grok-3 on February 17, 2025, positioning it as the company's most advanced AI model to date, with enhanced reasoning capabilities integrated with broad pretraining knowledge. The model was unveiled during a livestream event on X, where demonstrations included complex tasks such as plotting interplanetary trajectories. Elon Musk described Grok-3 as an order of magnitude more capable than its predecessor, Grok-2, emphasizing its competitive edge against models from OpenAI and DeepSeek.

Grok-3 was trained on xAI’s Colossus cluster in Memphis, which reporting described as expanding from about 100,000 NVIDIA H100 GPUs to around 200,000 GPUs. Musk said pretraining used about 10 times the compute of Grok-2. xAI said this supported stronger reasoning, especially in mathematics, science, and coding, including what it called graduate-level expert reasoning on GPQA. xAI also reported that an early Grok-3 version reached an Elo score of 1402 on the LMArena Chatbot Arena, a human-preference leaderboard.

On standardized tests, xAI reported that non-reasoning Grok-3 outperformed OpenAI’s GPT-4o on benchmarks including AIME 2024 and GPQA, while Grok-3 reasoning variants scored higher than OpenAI’s o3-mini-high on AIME 2025.

New features included DeepSearch, an agent for searching the web and X and synthesizing reports, and Think mode for extra test-time reasoning, with real-time data used in research and coding tasks. Voice mode was delayed from launch night and slated for about a week later; xAI also said the model would keep improving with frequent updates. xAI made Grok-3 accessible via its API in subsequent months, offering variants like Grok-3 Mini for lighter reasoning tasks.

#Grok-4 (July 2025)

Elon Musk announcing the release of Grok-4 during the xAI livestream event

xAI released Grok-4 on July 9, 2025, positioning it as the company's flagship AI model and claiming it to be the world's most intelligent system at the time of launch. The announcement occurred during a livestream event, where xAI highlighted Grok-4's superior performance across academic benchmarks, including top scores on the ARC-AGI evaluation, which tests abstract reasoning capabilities. This model succeeded Grok-3 and incorporated advancements in native tool usage, real-time web search integration, and multimodal processing encompassing language, vision, and coding tasks.

Access to Grok-4 was initially available to SuperGrok and Premium+ subscribers on the X platform as well as through the xAI API, with inference pricing at launch matching Grok-3 at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, maintaining high performance; detailed training data corpora and parameter counts remained undisclosed as of the release.

Post-launch evaluations by xAI and Elon Musk asserted that Grok-4 achieved postgraduate-level proficiency in numerous domains, surpassing human PhD expertise in specialized tasks but occasionally faltering in common-sense reasoning. Musk specifically noted its superiority to tools like Cursor for code debugging and generation. By September 2025, rollout expansions included broader integration for enterprise use, with ongoing enhancements to agentic capabilities, though independent third-party audits of benchmark claims were limited at that stage. xAI released extensions such as video generation with Grok Imagine in October 2025, building on Grok-4's foundational architecture.

#Grok-4 Heavy (July 2025)

Grok-4 Heavy was released alongside Grok-4 on July 9, 2025, as a multi-agent configuration of the same base model that uses parallel test-time compute. Multiple Grok-4 agents work independently on a query, explore different hypotheses, then compare outputs and synthesize a final answer (described by xAI as a “study group”). In the consumer Grok apps (grok.com, iOS, and Android), SuperGrok Heavy subscribers can select Heavy mode for complex reasoning, research, or high-stakes tasks; the mode has higher latency (often several minutes) and compute cost than the single-agent base model. Access was offered exclusively via the $300 monthly SuperGrok Heavy tier.
xAI-reported launch benchmarks showed the largest gains on hard reasoning sets relative to standard Grok-4: 100% versus 91.7% on AIME 2025, 50.7% versus 41.0% (with tools) on Humanity's Last Exam (the first model to exceed 50% on that exam), 61.9% versus 37.5% on USAMO 2025 proofs, 96.7% versus 90.0% on HMMT 2025, and 88.9% versus 87.5% on GPQA; differences were smaller on LiveCodeBench.

#Grok Code Fast 1 (August 2025)

xAI released Grok Code Fast 1 on August 28, 2025, a specialized coding-focused model optimized for agentic coding workflows and high-volume tasks across languages including Python and TypeScript. It excels in integration with code editors and development environments, available via the xAI API at competitive pricing for efficient software development applications.

#Grok-4 Fast (September 2025)

Grok-4 Fast was released on September 19, 2025, offering comparable performance to Grok-4 with improved efficiency and lower token costs of $0.20 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens.

#Grok-4.1 (November 2025)

xAI released Grok-4.1 on November 17, 2025, as an update to Grok-4 featuring improved reasoning, fewer hallucinations, and the #1 ranking on LMSYS Arena, along with enhancements in real-world usability, creativity, and accuracy, including strong performance in EQ-Bench for emotional intelligence evaluation and gains in creative writing, achieved through targeted post-training efforts focusing on factual accuracy for information-seeking queries, addressing limitations in fast non-reasoning models (limited reasoning depth and tool-call budgets), and incorporating large-scale reinforcement learning (RL) along with new agentic reward models. However, per xAI's model evaluations, Grok-4.1 shows higher sycophancy (excessive agreeableness or flattery) and deception scores than its predecessor Grok-4.

#Grok-4.1 Fast (November 2025)

xAI released Grok-4.1 Fast on November 19, 2025, available via its API in two variants: grok-4-1-fast-reasoning for maximal intelligence and grok-4-1-fast-non-reasoning for efficiency. Positioned as the company's best tool-calling model with enhanced search and multimodal reasoning, it offers strong reasoning capabilities for agentic tasks and supports a 2 million token context window.

#Grok Imagine (January 2026)

Grok Imagine was initially released as version 0.9 in October 2025. xAI announced the Grok Imagine API on January 28, 2026, a powerful tool for video and image generation including text-to-video, image-to-video, and advanced editing features, for end-to-end creative workflows. Version 1.0, released on February 2, 2026, enhanced capabilities to include 10-second videos at 720p resolution with improved audio. Ongoing enhancements to Grok Imagine models in February 2026 included achieving #1 in Video Arena.

#Grok-4.20 (February/March 2026)

Grok 4.20 was xAI's flagship model as of March 2026, released in beta on February 17, 2026, with API availability starting March 10, 2026, and full integration into user modes (Auto, Fast, Expert, Heavy) by mid-March. It features industry-leading speed, agentic tool calling, a 2,000,000 token context window in variants, the lowest hallucination rate on the market, and strict prompt adherence for precise, truthful responses.

Grok 4.20 introduces a unique four-agent parallel processing architecture: a central Grok agent coordinates overall response and task decomposition/synthesis; Harper handles fact-checking and real-time X data integration; Benjamin manages logic, mathematics, and coding tasks; and Lucas covers creative reasoning and contrarian perspectives. These agents work in parallel, debate internally, and aggregate consensus, significantly reducing hallucinations and enhancing performance on complex tasks.

API model IDs include grok-4.20-0309-reasoning, grok-4.20-0309-non-reasoning, and grok-4.20-multi-agent-0309, priced at $2.00 input / $6.00 output per million tokens with defined rate limits.

#Grok-4.20 Heavy (February 2026)

Grok-4.20 Heavy is in early access/coming soon for Heavy subscribers as of March 2026. It scales the multi-agent system to 16 specialized agents collaborating in real-time for enhanced handling of complex tasks, building on the base model's 4-agent framework. In the consumer apps, SuperGrok Heavy users select Heavy mode (alongside Auto, Fast, and Expert) to invoke this higher-compute parallel reasoning for difficult queries.

#Open-source status

The current Grok chatbot, powered by frontier models such as Grok-4.7 as of October 2026, is proprietary and not open source; users access it via the grok.com website, apps, or X platform integration, but cannot download or self-host the underlying model weights for the live version.

xAI has released model weights for select older Grok versions:

Grok-1 (March 17, 2024): Full base model weights and architecture released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license, available on GitHub and Hugging Face. This remains the most fully open release.

Grok-2/Grok-2.5 (August 24, 2025): Model weights released on Hugging Face (xai-org/grok-2) under the custom Grok 2 Community License Agreement. The license permits commercial and non-commercial use but is revocable, prohibits using the model to train or improve other AI models, and requires attribution. Critics, including analyses from ZDNet, have described this as "open-washing" because the restrictions limit true open-source freedoms (e.g., no full training code or datasets, and competitive-use bans), distinguishing it from unrestricted open-source models.

Elon Musk stated in August 2025 that Grok-3 would be made open source in about six months (around February 2026) and reconfirmed the plan in February 2026, but as of October 2026 Grok-3, Grok-4, Grok-4.7 and subsequent models remain proprietary with no public weights release.

This mixed approach reflects xAI's emphasis on openness for older models to foster research while protecting frontier capabilities for competitive and safety reasons.

#Recent updates (March 2026)

In March 2026, xAI introduced several user-facing updates to Grok. A new "Workspace" feature was added to the desktop version (grok.com) to improve organization of chats and generated content. The Grok Imagine tool received a major UI overhaul, making text-to-video generation significantly faster and more intuitive, with additional stylized templates such as "Chibi" that gained viral attention. These changes contribute to a refreshed, smoother user interface across platforms. Ongoing point releases in the Grok 4.20 beta continued through March, including fixes for instruction following, hallucinations, LaTeX support, and multi-image rendering.

#Grok-5 (Anticipated Q2 2026)

xAI has announced plans for Grok-5, a 6-trillion-parameter model originally anticipated for release in Q2 2026 and trained using the Colossus 2 supercomputer, the world's first gigawatt-scale data center. As of October 2026 it remains in training with no official release date announced. Elon Musk stated that Grok-5 has a 10% chance of achieving artificial general intelligence (AGI). The model is expected to include advanced multimodal capabilities, such as real-time video processing and understanding. Planned applications encompass using Grok-5 to play complex games like League of Legends to advance AGI development, generating AI-driven games through xAI's gaming initiatives, and integration into AI agent systems like Macrohard for software development, optimization, and simulating entire software companies.

#Technical Architecture

#Training Infrastructure and Compute

xAI built a custom distributed training and inference stack based on JAX, Rust, and Kubernetes to develop and serve Grok models. This framework enables efficient management of massive GPU clusters, such as the Colossus supercomputer, by handling worker scheduling, containerization, fault tolerance, and long-running distributed jobs essential for large-scale AI training and real-time inference.
xAI built the Colossus supercomputer cluster in a repurposed Electrolux factory in Memphis, Tennessee. It became operational in 122 days and was the world's largest AI training system at launch. The initial setup used 100,000 NVIDIA H100 GPUs. The cluster was subsequently doubled to 200,000 GPUs. This infrastructure powered pretraining and refinement for Grok-3, released in February 2025, providing over 200 million GPU-hours of compute.

xAI used the 200,000-GPU Colossus cluster for Grok-4 training, released in July 2025. This included large-scale reinforcement learning to improve reasoning and native tool use. xAI also used Oracle Cloud Infrastructure for additional training and inference on later Grok models. OCI's scalable AI compute instances supplemented Colossus's on-site power.

Grok-1, released in November 2023, used smaller compute resources. Estimates place it at about 10^{23} to 10^{24} floating-point operations (FLOPs), a measure of computational effort. This reflected xAI's early efforts before full Colossus use. By Grok-3, needs grew to around 10^{26} FLOPs. This highlights the exponential compute scaling for advanced models. xAI focuses on in-house hardware control. This reduces latency and costs from third-party clouds. In Memphis, though, power demands and gas turbine emissions have raised local environmental concerns. Plans call for expanding Colossus to 1 million GPUs. This will support ongoing training for Grok-4, Grok-5, and future models.
Training large Grok models incurs substantial compute costs. For instance, Epoch AI estimated the training of Grok-4 at approximately $490 million, involving massive energy use (310 million kWh) and resources via the Colossus cluster.

Ongoing inference costs for serving Grok to millions of users represent the primary daily operational expense. Industry-wide, inference can account for 60-80%+ of lifecycle costs for popular models. With Colossus's power draw reaching 300 MW (plus on-site generation), daily electricity and ops costs are estimated in the hundreds of thousands to millions of dollars range, depending on utilization and scale, though exact figures remain proprietary to xAI.
Subsequent versions have scaled significantly: Grok 4.20 (released March 2026) is estimated at 1.7–3 trillion parameters in MoE architecture; Grok 4.7 is the current flagship as of October 2026; Grok 5 (in training) around 6 trillion parameters.

Grok-1, released in November 2023, has 314 billion parameters in a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture. MoE uses multiple specialized sub-models, or "experts," with only a subset active per input. This model has 8 experts total, activating 2 per token for sparse activation—about 25% of weights—which improves efficiency during inference. The design cuts active computation compared to dense models of similar scale, while preserving performance on benchmarks like math and coding tasks. xAI trained Grok-1 from scratch with a custom stack, without external foundation models. It emphasized broad pretraining on diverse internet-scale data to build general capabilities.

xAI has not disclosed parameter counts for later models. Community analysis of a Grok-2 checkpoint on Hugging Face—distinct from the August 2025 open-source Grok-2.5 release—estimated about 270 billion parameters in an MoE architecture. Counts for Grok-1.5 (March 2024), Grok-3 (February 2025), and Grok-4 (July 2025) remain secret. Internal scaling points to larger sizes and more training compute for improved reasoning and multimodal features. #Training, Updates, and Adaptation

Grok's core large language model is trained on a large, fixed dataset with a knowledge cutoff date (reported as around November 2024 for models such as Grok-3 and Grok-4; subsequent releases have later cutoffs, such as May 2026 for Grok 4.7). Unlike hypothetical continuously learning systems, Grok does not update its neural network weights in real-time based on individual user conversations. This design choice prevents issues like catastrophic forgetting (where new information overwrites prior knowledge), model instability, and privacy risks associated with incorporating personal user data directly into the core parameters.

Instead, Grok achieves adaptation and up-to-date responses through several mechanisms:

In-conversation adaptation: Grok maintains full context across multi-turn interactions, allowing it to reference prior messages, refine responses based on user tone/preferences, and build on the ongoing dialogue dynamically.

Real-time external retrieval: Grok integrates tools for web searches, browsing pages, accessing real-time public X posts, and other live data sources. This enables responses informed by current events and information beyond the training cutoff, functioning similarly to retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems.

System-level improvements: xAI continuously refines Grok through periodic new model releases (e.g., iterative versions like Grok-4 to Grok-4.20), fine-tuning on aggregated, anonymized, or opted-in usage data, reinforcement learning from human/AI feedback, and rapid development cycles. Public statements and reports suggest some later iterations incorporate ongoing reinforcement learning loops, enabling noticeable improvements over short periods (e.g., weekly updates or continuous refinement pipelines on xAI servers).

This architecture ensures Grok remains reliable, grounded in its pre-trained knowledge, and capable of freshness via external means and periodic upgrades, while avoiding the risks of unchecked real-time parameter adaptation from user interactions.

There is no centralized official public gallery equivalent to OpenAI's GPT Store, though Grok Bots (launched August 2026) can be shared via portable links and independent directories.

Custom Instructions: Accessible via the Custom preset in response style options (alongside Concise, Formal, and Socratic). Users set persistent guidelines in settings (e.g., "Always respond from a biblical Christian perspective, citing Scripture") that apply across conversations without repetition. This enables semi-tuned experiences for recurring topics.

Custom Agents: Launched March 2026, users create up to four named specialist personas (each with up to 4,000-character instructions) via Settings → Customize → Create Agent. Agents can be invoked by name and provide more persistent specialized versions than one-off prompting.

Grok Skills: Launched May 2026, users create persistent reusable task workflows via conversation, file upload, or the Skill Creator; they are invocable with slash commands and support sharing.

Prompt-based Personas: Users can instruct Grok in-chat to adopt roles, such as "Act as a Christian theologian specializing in the Bible" or "Be a Bible study companion." Grok adapts tone, depth, and references accordingly for the session, though not as persistently as dedicated instances unless combined with custom instructions, agents, or memory.

Memory Feature: Enabled in settings (added April 2025), Grok recalls key details and preferences (e.g., preferred Bible translation or worldview) from past interactions for more consistent personalization across separate chats.

Workspaces/Projects: On grok.com (and partially in apps), users create dedicated spaces for ongoing topics. These support file uploads (e.g., Bible PDFs, study notes), per-space instructions, and focused context.

Additionally, Grok includes built-in Companions (launched July 2025) as predefined specialized personas with avatars, voice, and adaptive behaviors (e.g., flirtatious or thematic), but these are not user-customizable for arbitrary topics like theology.

These tools allow effective niche use (e.g., Christian-specific queries) through configuration and prompting, leveraging Grok's truth-seeking design for deep engagement without heavy filtering. Grok Bots add autonomous, shareable agent capabilities with dedicated compute. For a centralized public marketplace of chat-shaped specialized AIs, competitors like ChatGPT historically offered advantages via their Custom GPT ecosystem.
